info.title: ExecuTorch Bencher API
info.description: Internal LLM benchmark collection and analysis service for Android phones and Linux hosts. Provides HTTP endpoints to ingest, store, and retrieve benchmark run results, content-addressed artifacts, and registered model assets. The service has no authentication and is meant for a trusted lab network.

post.summary:
Stream and store an artifact's content, deduplicating by SHA-256. The
body is the raw artifact bytes, streamed directly - **not** a multipart
form. `kind` and `original_name` are query parameters.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: The artifact's kind. Determines whether the content is stored Zstandard-compressed (see `ArtifactKind`).

parameters.name: original_name
parameters.description: Caller-supplied display name, retained only as metadata.

requestBody.description: Raw artifact bytes, streamed directly. Rejected once the stream exceeds the server's configured maximum artifact upload size.

201.description: The artifact was stored, or an identical one (by SHA-256) already existed and was reused.

400.description: `kind` is not a recognized artifact kind.

413.description: The upload exceeds the server's configured maximum artifact size.

get.summary:
Stream an artifact's content, decompressing transparently if it is
stored Zstandard-compressed. The response body is the raw content with
its stored media type - never a JSON-encoded string.

200.description: The artifact's content, streamed with its stored media type (or `application/octet-stream` if none was recorded).

404.description: No artifact exists with this ID.

410.description: The database record exists but the file is missing on disk.

get.summary:
Like `content`, but sets `Content-Disposition: attachment` with a safe
filename derived from the artifact's kind and content hash.

200.description: The artifact's content as an attachment download.

404.description: No artifact exists with this ID.

410.description: The database record exists but the file is missing on disk.

get.summary:
Fetch an artifact's metadata, including whether its content-addressed
file is currently available on disk.

404.description: No artifact exists with this ID.

get.summary:
Stream change notifications as Server-Sent Events. Each event has an
`event` name, a process-scoped monotonically increasing `id`, and a
JSON `data` payload:
get.description:
- `run.created` - a run was recorded; `data` is a `RunCreatedEvent`.
- `artifact.created` - an artifact was stored; `data` is an
  `ArtifactCreatedEvent`.
- `model.registered` - a model asset was registered; `data` is a
  `ModelRegisteredEvent`.

A comment keep-alive is sent while idle (every 15 seconds by default).
Events are signals to re-fetch, not state: nothing is replayed after a
reconnect, and the REST operations remain authoritative. A subscriber
that falls too far behind is disconnected and should reconnect and
re-fetch.

200.description: An open `text/event-stream`. Event names: `run.created` (data: `RunCreatedEvent`), `artifact.created` (data: `ArtifactCreatedEvent`), `model.registered` (data: `ModelRegisteredEvent`). Keep-alive comments are sent while idle; missed events are not replayed.

get.summary:
List registered model assets, optionally narrowed to one content hash.
Not paginated - matches the current implementation's real, unpaginated
response shape. See `specs/ingestion-service` - "Service exposes model
lookup by content hash".

parameters.name: sha256
parameters.description:
Return only the model asset with this content hash (lowercase
64-character hexadecimal SHA-256), so a collector that knows a
model file's hash can find its asset ID. An empty list when no
asset matches.

200.description: The matching model assets (all of them without a filter).

post.summary:
Register an external `.pte` model file by path, without copying it.
Registering a file whose SHA-256 already matches a registered model
reuses the cached checksum and existing record rather than rehashing or
duplicating it.

201.description: The model was registered, or an existing record with the same SHA-256 was reused.

400.description: The body is not valid JSON, or the path is not absolute, does not name a `.pte` file, does not exist, is not a regular file, or lies outside every registrable model root. `details.field` is `path`.

get.summary: Fetch a single registered model asset by ID.

404.description: No model asset exists with this ID.

post.summary:
Trigger explicit full verification of a model's checksum: recalculates
its SHA-256 from the current file content, updates its last-verified
timestamp, and reports whether it still matches the registered value.
Only implemented for external-mode models.

200.description: Verification completed; the asset's cached checksum, availability, and last-verified timestamp were refreshed.

404.description: No model asset exists with this ID.

501.description: Verification for managed-mode models is not yet implemented.

get.summary:
Group runs into benchmark configurations and report each one's
median/min/max/n throughput over succeeded runs, plus failure and
throttling counts. Rows are ordered by commit timestamp (falling back to
first run time) descending. At most 500 rows are returned.

parameters.name: host_accelerator
parameters.description: The accelerator as the runtime backend reports it.

parameters.name: prompt_sha256
parameters.description: Lowercase 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the prompt.

get.summary:
List runs newest first, with exact-match filters and opaque keyset
pagination. See `specs/ingestion-service` - "Service exposes a
paginated, filterable run listing".

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: host_accelerator
parameters.description:
The accelerator as the runtime backend reports it (Vulkan device
name on Linux, GPU on Android).

parameters.name: prompt_sha256
parameters.description: Lowercase 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the prompt.

200.description: One page of run summaries, newest first.

400.description: An unrecognized enum filter value, an out-of-range `limit`, or an undecodable `cursor`.

post.summary:
Record one complete run attempt. The body mirrors the run response;
enumerated fields take their documented string values. Validation
failures name the field in `details.field`; a run ID that already exists
is rejected with `409 conflict` and left unchanged, so a client that
lost a response may retry and then confirm with `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}`.
See `specs/ingestion-service` - "Service accepts complete run records
over HTTP".

201.description: The run was stored; the body is what `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}` returns.

400.description: The body is not valid JSON, a field is invalid, the snapshot does not match the platform and device class, or a referenced model asset or artifact does not exist. `details.field` names the field.

409.description: A run with this ID already exists; it is unchanged.

413.description: The body exceeds the maximum run record size (2 MiB).

get.summary:
Fetch a run by ID, including its outcome and the artifacts/model it
referenced. See `specs/ingestion-service` - "Run responses expose
viewable artifact metadata".

404.description: No run exists with this ID.

get.summary: Report API and schema compatibility information.
Reports whether the service is running and able to reach its database.

200.description: The service and its database connection are healthy.

503.description: The service cannot reach its database.

code.description:
Stable, machine-readable failure category. Current values: `invalid_request`,
`not_found`, `artifact_file_missing`, `payload_too_large`, `conflict`,
`not_implemented`, `internal_error`. This field is an open string, not a
closed enum - new categories may be added as the API grows.

message.description:
Human-readable description of the failure. Not guaranteed stable across
versions or releases - match on `code`, not this text.
message.example: gpu_clock_mhz must be greater than zero

details.description: Optional structured context about the failure, e.g. which field was invalid.

request_id.description: Opaque identifier correlating this error with server-side logs, when available.

ApiErrorResponse.description: The consistent JSON envelope every rejected or failed request responds with.

sha256.description: Lowercase 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the content.

ArtifactKind.description:
The kinds of files the backend manages as content-addressed artifacts.
See `specs/benchmark-schema` - "Large inputs and outputs are tracked as
content-addressed artifacts".

ArtifactMetadataResponse.description: An artifact's full metadata, including where to fetch its content.

sha256.description:
Lowercase 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the original,
uncompressed content.

available.description:
Whether the content-addressed file still exists on disk. `false`
means the database record exists but the file is unavailable - see
the `artifact_file_missing` error on `content`/`download`.

ArtifactView.description:
A referenced artifact's viewable metadata: enough to know whether it is
present and how to retrieve it, without a separate lookup.

original_filename.description:
Caller-supplied display name at upload time; never used to choose a
storage path. Absent when no name was supplied.

media_type.description: MIME type captured from the upload's `Content-Type` header, if any.

available.description:
Whether the content-addressed file still exists on disk. The
database record can outlive the file (see `artifact_file_missing`
errors on content/download).

BinaryBody.description:
OpenAPI-only marker for a raw, unstructured binary body (streamed as
`application/octet-stream`, not JSON and not a multipart form).

Compression.description:
How an artifact's stored bytes relate to its recorded content: `None`
means the stored file *is* the original content; `Zstd` means the stored
file is a Zstandard-compressed encoding of it. The recorded `sha256`
always identifies the original, uncompressed content either way.

CorrectnessResult.description:
A run's correctness-validation outcome, independent of `ExitStatus`. See
`specs/benchmark-schema` - "Correctness validation is tracked
independently of process exit status".

CreateRunRequest.description:
One complete run attempt, as a collector submits it. Field names,
units, nullability, and enumerations match `RunResponse`; the artifact
references are IDs returned by `POST /api/v1/artifacts`, and
`model_asset_id` comes from `GET /api/v1/models?sha256=...` or
`POST /api/v1/models/register`.

id.description:
Client-assigned run ID (a UUID; v7 recommended so IDs sort by
time). Posting the same ID twice is rejected with `409 conflict`.

finished_at.description: Null when the run never finished (crash, reboot, timeout).

repetition.description: Zero-based repetition index within the run's batch.

env_vars.description:
Captured environment-variable allowlist as a JSON object (`null` =
unset, `""` = empty).

device_class.description:
One of the stable `DeviceClass` values. `internal` requires the
complete Android lab snapshot; `external` records what the host can
report.

device_model.description: Product/model name as the host reports it.

device_uptime_seconds.description: Host uptime at run start, in seconds.

initial_temperature_celsius.description: Device temperature at run start, in degrees Celsius. Android only.

max_temperature_celsius.description:
Maximum device temperature observed, in degrees Celsius. Android
only.

host_os.description:
OS release: distribution and version on Linux, Android release and
build id on phones.

host_cpu_model.description: CPU model on Linux, SoC model on Android.

host_accelerator.description:
The accelerator the runtime backend executed on, as the backend
reports it.

executable_sha256.description:
Lowercase 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the executable.
Null when the binary's identity was not preserved; never a
placeholder.

prompt_sha256.description: Lowercase 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the prompt.

prefill_tokens_per_sec.description:
Prefill throughput in tokens per second (0 when nothing was
measured).

decode_tokens_per_sec.description:
Decode throughput in tokens per second. Null when the run recorded
no decode measurement.

output_preview.description:
Truncated server-side to the configured preview length; the output
artifact holds the complete text.

DeviceClass.description:
Whether a host is a lab device under full control or an external one.
Internal devices (rooted development phones with SUMD/BSP/clock control)
must carry the rigorous Android snapshot; external hosts (retail phones,
any Linux box) record whatever they can report. See
`specs/benchmark-schema` - "Host state is captured as a
platform-specific immutable snapshot".

ExitStatus.description:
A run's process-level outcome. See `specs/benchmark-schema` - "A run
captures process-level outcome data".

FacetsResponse.description: Distinct filter values across all runs, ignoring the active filters.

MetricStatsResponse.description:
Median, minimum, maximum, and sample count of one throughput metric,
in tokens per second, over succeeded runs.

n.description: Number of succeeded runs the statistic was computed over.

ModelAssetRef.description: The model a run exercised, as referenced from a run summary.

sha256.description: Lowercase 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the model file.

external_path.description:
The server-side filesystem path this external model was registered
from. `null` for managed-mode models. Currently returned to every
caller as-is - no authentication exists in this service to restrict
it to authorized clients.

last_verified_at.description: Absent until the model has been explicitly verified at least once.

available.description: Whether the registered file currently resolves on disk.

ModelAssetSummary.description: A run's referenced model asset, summarized for display alongside the run.

sha256.description: Lowercase 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the model file.

available.description:
Whether the model is currently available (registered file still
resolves on disk).

sha256.description: Lowercase 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the model file.

Platform.description:
The kind of host a run executed on. Selects which host-state snapshot a
run carries. See `specs/benchmark-schema` - "Host state is captured as a
platform-specific immutable snapshot".

path.description:
Absolute path to an existing `.pte` file on the server's filesystem,
beneath one of the server's registrable model roots
(`MODEL_REGISTER_ROOTS`, default the model root). Symlinks are
resolved before the root check, so neither `..` nor a symlink can
escape a root. External mode never copies this file - see
`specs/artifact-storage` - "External model assets are registered
once without copying". Registering the same file's SHA-256 again
reuses the cached checksum rather than rehashing or copying it.

ResultRowResponse.description: One benchmark configuration and its statistics over all its runs.

device_class.description: `internal`: lab device. `external`: retail phone or Linux box.

device_model.description: Product/model name as the host reports it. Null when not captured.

sumd_driver_version.description: Lab Android devices only; null elsewhere.

bsp_version.description: Lab Android devices only; null elsewhere.

gpu_clock_mhz.description: GPU clock in MHz. Lab Android devices only; null elsewhere.

mif_clock_mhz.description:
MIF (memory interface) clock in MHz. Lab Android devices only; null
elsewhere.

int_clock_mhz.description:
INT (interconnect) clock in MHz. Lab Android devices only; null
elsewhere.

host_accelerator.description:
The accelerator the runtime backend executed on. Null when not
captured.

prompt_sha256.description: Lowercase 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the prompt.

oneOf.description:
Prefill throughput statistics in tokens per second over succeeded
runs. Null when no run of this configuration succeeded.

Decode throughput statistics in tokens per second over succeeded
runs that recorded a decode measurement. Null when none did.

not_succeeded.description: Runs whose exit status is not `succeeded`.

correctness_failed.description: Succeeded runs whose correctness result is `failed`.

ResultsResponse.description: Grouped results: one row per configuration, newest commit first.

truncated.description:
True when more than the maximum number of configurations matched
and only the first 500 are returned.

RunCreatedEvent.description: `data` payload of a `run.created` event: the run's listing summary.

prefill_tokens_per_sec.description: Prefill throughput in tokens per second.

decode_tokens_per_sec.description: Decode throughput in tokens per second; null when not recorded.

RunListResponse.description: One page of run summaries, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Null when no more runs match.

RunResponse.description:
A run's complete recorded record: metadata, device state, performance
configuration, build/workload identity, results, and the artifacts and
model it referenced. Flat: every field is top-level, named as recorded,
with units in descriptions. See `specs/ingestion-service` - "Single-run
responses expose the complete recorded run".

finished_at.description: Absent while the run is still in progress.

correctness_result.description:
Independent of `exit_status` - a run can succeed but fail
correctness validation, or vice versa.

output_preview.description: Absent when the run produced no output or has not finished.

repetition.description: Zero-based repetition index within the run's batch.

command_args.description: The exact command-line argument array, as a JSON array of strings.

command_line.description: Human-readable command line. Absent when not recorded.

input_parameters.description: Caller-defined input parameters, as recorded JSON.

env_vars.description:
Captured environment-variable allowlist, as a JSON object mapping
variable name to its value (`null` = unset, `""` = empty).

device_class.description:
`internal`: lab device under full control, rigorous Android snapshot
required. `external`: retail phone or Linux box recording what it can
report; unavailable fields are null.

device_model.description: Product/model name as the host reports it. Null when not captured.

device_uptime_seconds.description: Host uptime at run start, in seconds. Null when not captured.

bsp_version.description: Lab Android devices only; null elsewhere.

sumd_driver_version.description: Lab Android devices only; null elsewhere.

battery_charging.description: Android only; null when not captured.

initial_temperature_celsius.description:
Device temperature at run start, in degrees Celsius. Android only;
null when not captured.

max_temperature_celsius.description:
Maximum device temperature observed during the run, in degrees
Celsius. Android only; null when not captured.

gpu_clock_mhz.description: GPU clock in MHz. Lab Android devices only; null elsewhere.

mif_clock_mhz.description:
MIF (memory interface) clock in MHz. Lab Android devices only; null
elsewhere.

int_clock_mhz.description:
INT (interconnect) clock in MHz. Lab Android devices only; null
elsewhere.

host_os.description:
OS release: distribution and version on Linux, Android release and
build id on phones. Null when not captured.

host_kernel.description: Kernel release. Null when not captured.

host_cpu_model.description: CPU model on Linux, SoC model on Android. Null when not captured.

host_cpu_count.description: Logical CPU count. Null when not captured.

host_memory_bytes.description: Total memory in bytes. Null when not captured.

host_accelerator.description:
The accelerator the runtime backend executed on, as the backend
reports it (Vulkan device on Linux, GPU on Android). Null when not
captured.

host_accelerator_driver.description: The accelerator's driver version. Null when not captured.

git_branch.description: Git branch the run was made from. Absent when not recorded.

git_commit_timestamp.description: The commit's timestamp. Absent when not recorded.

git_commit_subject.description: The commit's subject line. Absent when not recorded.

executable_sha256.description:
Lowercase 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the executable.
Null when the binary's identity was not preserved.

prompt_sha256.description: Lowercase 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the prompt.

prefill_tokens_per_sec.description: Prefill throughput in tokens per second.

decode_tokens_per_sec.description:
Decode throughput in tokens per second. Null when the run recorded
no decode measurement.

error_summary.description: Short description of the failure. Absent when the run did not fail.

RunSummaryResponse.description:
One run's list-view summary: identity, configuration, outcome, and
throughput. Fetch `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}` for the complete record.

finished_at.description: Absent while the run is still in progress.

device_class.description:
`internal`: lab device with the rigorous snapshot. `external`:
retail phone or Linux box recording what it can report.

device_model.description: Product/model name as the host reports it. Null when not captured.

git_branch.description: Absent when the collector did not record it.

sumd_driver_version.description: Lab Android devices only; null elsewhere.

bsp_version.description: Lab Android devices only; null elsewhere.

host_accelerator.description: The accelerator the backend executed on. Null when not captured.

prefill_tokens_per_sec.description: Prefill throughput in tokens per second.

decode_tokens_per_sec.description:
Decode throughput in tokens per second. Null when the run recorded
no decode measurement.

thermal_throttling.description: Null when the platform's collector did not capture it.

UploadResponse.description: Result of a successful artifact upload.

sha256.description:
Lowercase 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the original,
uncompressed content.

compression.description:
How the stored bytes relate to the original content. `sha256` and
`size_bytes` always describe the original, uncompressed content
either way.

api_version.description:
The documented OpenAPI contract's version. Bumped by hand when the
contract changes in a way clients should notice.

server_version.description:
The running server binary's Cargo package version
(`CARGO_PKG_VERSION`), not duplicated by hand.

minimum_runner_version.description:
The oldest Python benchmark runner version known to be compatible
with this server. Maintained by hand; no runner exists yet to
validate against.

schema_version.description:
Increments only on a backward-incompatible change to the run/
artifact/model database or contract schema.
